designs.title: Fanad Head Lighthouse
designs.why: Classic poster hierarchy: the arched condensed serif heading sits well with the spaced country and LIGHTHOUSE lines, the ruled data columns frame the tower, and the cliff engraving has real depth. But the bottom half is a near-solid mass of hatching that turns into a heavy block of ink on the black tee, the left data column (three entries) outweighs the right, and there is a small rule glitch under the bottom frame line.
designs.fix: Open up the foreground hatching in the lower third (more white in the rocks and sea) so the tower stays the focal point and the print is less of an ink slab. While doing that, clean up the bottom-frame blemish.

designs.title: Portland Head Light
designs.why: Nice asymmetric scene, with the keeper's house balancing the tower on the right and a strong arched heading. But PORTLAND HEAD is set so wide that its letters nearly touch the inner frame, so the header feels cramped next to the airy sides of the other prints. The data mixes long and short lines unevenly ('CONSTRUCTED 1787–1790' vs. 'U.S. NATIONAL REGISTER' filler).
designs.fix: Shrink or track the heading so there is at least one cap-width of margin from the frame, and trim the data to two even blocks (dates left, coordinates right).

designs.title: Cape Agulhas Lighthouse
designs.why: The cleanest of the set: one big arched heading, two short symmetric data blocks, and a centred banded tower that reads instantly from 3 m. The striped tower gives a bold silhouette, and the sky leaves breathing room so the engraving and the type don't compete.
designs.fix: Add a small spaced 'LIGHTHOUSE' line with rules under the heading, as the series does elsewhere, to anchor the arch and keep the set consistent. Also lighten the dense bottom-left rock hatching a touch.

designs.title: Phare de Saint-Mathieu
designs.why: The abbey ruins make the most interesting scene in the series, but the header stacks four tiers (FRANCE / PHARE DE / SAINT-MATHIEU / place line), and PHARE DE at a smaller size reads as a weak, crowded preamble. Data sits only on the left, so the top right is empty and the top half is lopsided.
designs.fix: Simplify the header to SAINT-MATHIEU as the single arched hero, with 'PHARE DE' folded into the small spaced line above it. Then move the coordinates into a right-hand data block to balance the columns.
